title: KV hotspot gating with probabilistic repack and decode smoothing
creator: Asha Mehta
description:
Summary: Reduce p95/p99 decode tail latency and eviction churn under bursty traffic by (1) quickly detecting short-lived KV hotspots using a lightweight time-decayed counter & gating mechanism, (2) applying a low-cost probabilistic repack (background slot consolidation) when hotspots persist, and (3) smoothing decode admission to avoid prefill storms that cause thrashing.

Background: We see frequent short bursts from chat-style workloads where a small subset of token spans becomes hot for a few hundred milliseconds and then cools. Current LRU-style reclamation plus eager background compaction causes concurrent repacks and aggressive kernel migration, which increases tail latency and spikes GPU memory copy activity. Existing work (see related ENG tickets) focuses on long-lived residency policies and complex reservation auctions; this ticket targets the fast-path: fast detection + cheap consolidation + admission smoothing.

Proposal:
- Hotspot detection: maintain per-shard lightweight exponential-decay counters keyed by KV page ID (64-bit). Counters are updated on prefill hits and decode accesses. When counter > gate_threshold, the page enters a gated-hot state for gate_ttl ms. Gating throttles eviction and pins a small soft-reserve for the page to avoid immediate eviction during the burst.
- Probabilistic repack: when gated-hot pages exceed a configurable fraction of shard capacity and observed fragmentation > frag_threshold, schedule a background probabilistic repack that samples low-benefit slots for consolidation instead of full compaction. Repack is rate-limited by an eviction_budget token-bucket to avoid competing with foreground decode.
- Decode smoothing (admission): implement a token-slope limiter per-tenant that spreads decode starts over a short window (50-200ms) based on recent start-rate. This prevents synchronized prefill floods that amplify eviction cascades. The limiter reports backpressure signals to the router so requests can be routed to fallback kernels or lower-cost model variants.
- Kernel routing hints: expose gated-hot hint to the kernel scheduler so it can prefer kernels with smaller working set (compact-kernel) for decodes touching gated pages, reducing KV read amplification.

Metrics: primary metrics are p95/p99 decode latency, background repack GPU memory copy throughput, eviction churn (evictions/sec), fragmentation score (0..1), and work-stealing incidence. Goal: reduce p99 decode tail by 25% and eviction churn by 40% on bursty chat traces while keeping average throughput within 5% of baseline.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Risk of over-pinning: gating could increase steady-state memory usage if thresholds are too lenient. Mitigation: gated-hot uses a soft-reserve and auto-evicts after gate_ttl with conservative backoff.
- Complexity: probabilistic repack introduces new background activity; keep implementation bounded (sampled slots, single-threaded repack worker per-shard).
- Telemetry cost: per-page counters add dimension cards—we will aggregate counters by heat-buckets to limit cardinality.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Simulation harness: extend existing prefill/eviction simulator to emulate gated-hot and probabilistic repack (2 weeks).
2) Instrumentation + feature flags: add decay counters and gate state, implement token-slope limiter in router (1 week).
3) Repack worker + kernel hint path: implement background probabilistic repack and expose kernel hint (2 weeks).
4) Canary rollout and metrics: run on canary pool with chaos tests and perf dashboards (1-2 weeks).

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria field.

Notes: coordinate with SDK team for diagnostic flags and ensure canary tenants can opt-out via route policy.
acceptance_criteria: p99 decode latency decreases by >=25% on bursty chat trace in canary compared to baseline
eviction churn reduces by >=40% under the same trace
background repack GPU copy bandwidth remains below configured eviction_budget during steady traffic
no customer-visible OOMs in canary rollout; gated pages auto-evict after gate_ttl
end-to-end unit and integration tests for gate lifecycle, repack worker, and token-slope limiter are added
technical_notes: use 8-bit decayed counters stored in shard metadata ringbuffer to limit memory; counters saturate at 255
gate_ttl default 300ms, backoff multiplier 2x per repeated gate entry within 10s window
probabilistic repack samples slots with low recent-access-weight; expected amortized cost is <1% of shard bandwidth
kernel hint transmitted as a 1-byte affinity flag in prefill descriptor to avoid protocol churn
token-slope limiter implemented as leaky bucket with adaptive slope parameter derived from recent 1s start-rate
